newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli woman accused of racism over pig poster.
newsitem.headline: Israeli woman accused of racism over pig poster.

text.p: Israeli prosecutors added racism on Monday to the charges facing a Jewish woman accused of putting up posters in Hebron which inflamed Arab anger by depicting the Prophet Mohammad as a pig.

Tatyana Suskin, a 26-year-old Israeli, is accused of committing a racist act, harming religious sensitivities, supporting a terrorist group and endangering life by stoning an Arab car -- offences that carry a maximum 26-year sentence.
According to a revised charge sheet made public on Monday, she acted with a racist motive. A charge of committing a racist act carries a maximum two-year sentence.

The posters -- pasted on June 27 across 20 storefronts on the Palestinian-ruled side of Hebron -- provoked an outpouring of Moslem ire and a surge in anti-Israeli protests in the volatile West Bank city.
Prosecutors have asked the Jerusalem District Court to order Suskin to remain in custody until the end of her trial. A hearing on the request is scheduled for Wednesday.

The charge sheet said she had worn the yellow shirt with a clenched fist symbolic of the outlawed anti-Arab Kach movement of the late Rabbi Meir Kahane when she put up the posters. It said the name "Kahane" was written across the shirt.

The indictment said Suskin hurled a stone at the car of a Palestinian motorist on June 28, breaking the rear left window and endangering human life on the road -- a charge carrying a maximum 20-year sentence.

Palestinians are frustrated over a peace process deadlocked since Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu began building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March. Netanyahu blames the violence on Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority.
